title: Cohomology on a quasi-compact open commutes with directed colimits of modules (Stacks 01FF, for schemes)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space has the following two properties: (1) the quasi-compact open subsets [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] form a basis of the topology, and (2) the intersection of any two quasi-compact open subsets is quasi-compact. Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), let $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ be a system of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules over $I$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] ($\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{i''i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_{i''i}$), and let $(\mathcal F,(c_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F)_{i\in I})$ be a colimit of this system in the category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ write $H^q(U,\mathcal G)=H^q(U,\mathcal G|_U)$ for the cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology] of the open subscheme $U$ with coefficients in the restriction $\mathcal G|_U$ ($W\mapsto\mathcal G(W)$ for opens $W\subseteq U$), and $H^q(U,h)$ for the map induced by a morphism $h$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Then for every quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$ and every $q\ge0$: (a) every $x\in H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ is of the form $H^q(U,c_i)(y)$ for some $i\in I$ and $y\in H^q(U,\mathcal F_i)$; (b) if $i\in I$ and $y\in H^q(U,\mathcal F_i)$ satisfy $H^q(U,c_i)(y)=0$, then $H^q(U,\varphi_{i'i})(y)=0$ for some $i'\ge i$. In other words, the canonical map $\varinjlim_iH^q(U,\mathcal F_i)\to H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ from the directed colimit of the abelian groups $H^q(U,\mathcal F_i)$, whose restriction to the $i$-th term is $H^q(U,c_i)$, is bijective.

proof.text: **Step 1 (cohomology of a quasi-compact open as derived functors; restriction to it).** Fix an open $U\subseteq X$. The open subscheme $U$ is a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $H^n(U,-)=R^nv_U$ ($n\ge0$) are the right derived functors of the global sections functor $v_U=\Gamma(U,-):\Mod(\mathcal O_U)\to\textit{Ab}$, $\mathcal A\mapsto\mathcal A(U)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive]; $v_U$ is additive and left exact because kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives] (applied to the scheme $U$). By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] the $R^nv_U$ form a $\delta$-functor: every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules has a long exact sequence $\cdots\to R^nv_U(\mathcal B)\to R^nv_U(\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{\delta^n}R^{n+1}v_U(\mathcal A)\to R^{n+1}v_U(\mathcal B)\to\cdots$ whose connecting maps commute with the maps induced by a morphism of short exact sequences; and $R^0v_U\cong v_U$ naturally. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives] (1), (2) the restriction functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_U$, is additive and exact and carries injective $\mathcal O_X$-modules to injective $\mathcal O_U$-modules, and by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (1) it carries a colimit cocone in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ to a colimit cocone in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$. Consequently, writing $H^n(U,\mathcal G)=H^n(U,\mathcal G|_U)$ and $H^n(U,h)$ as in the statement: (i) every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to0$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has a long exact sequence $\cdots\to H^n(U,\mathcal B)\to H^n(U,\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{\delta^n}H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal A)\to H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal B)\to\cdots$, and for a morphism $(a,b,c)$ of short exact sequences in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ one has $H^{n+1}(U,a)\circ\delta^n=\delta'^n\circ H^n(U,c)$ (apply the above to the restricted sequences and the restricted morphism); (ii) if $\mathcal I$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module then $H^n(U,\mathcal I)=0$ for $n>0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing], since $\mathcal I|_U$ is injective; (iii) $H^0(U,\mathcal G)\cong(\mathcal G|_U)(U)=\mathcal G(U)$, by isomorphisms $\theta_{\mathcal G}$ natural in $\mathcal G\in\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, so that $\theta_{\mathcal G'}\circ H^0(U,h)=h_U\circ\theta_{\mathcal G}$ for $h:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$. For $q\ge0$ let $P(q)$ be the assertion: for every quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$ and every directed system of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with a colimit in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, clauses (a) and (b) of the statement hold in degree $q$. As the source stresses, the induction is on $P(q)$, i.e. for all quasi-compact opens and all systems at once.

proof.text: **Step 2 (finite coverings of quasi-compact opens: Topology, Lemma 0069 (3), whose proof the source omits).** (i) A finite nonempty intersection $W_1\cap\cdots\cap W_r$ of quasi-compact opens of $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]: by induction on $r$, using hypothesis (2) for $(W_1\cap\cdots\cap W_{r-1})\cap W_r$. (ii) Let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open and $U=\bigcup_aV_a$ an open covering. For $x\in U$ choose $a$ with $x\in V_a$; since the quasi-compact opens form a basis (hypothesis (1)), there is a quasi-compact open $W_x$ with $x\in W_x\subseteq V_a$. The $W_x$ ($x\in U$) cover $U$, so finitely many $W_{x_1},\ldots,W_{x_m}$ do, since $U$ is quasi-compact. Thus $U=\bigcup_{j=1}^mU_j$, $U_j=W_{x_j}$, is a finite covering of $U$ by quasi-compact opens refining $(V_a)$, and by (i) every $U_{j_0\ldots j_p}=U_{j_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{j_p}$ is quasi-compact, in particular every $U_j\cap U_{j'}$. So $U$ has a cofinal system of open coverings $U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ with $J$ finite and all $U_j$, $U_j\cap U_{j'}$ (indeed all $U_{j_0\ldots j_p}$) quasi-compact. (If $U=\emptyset$ the empty covering, $m=0$, does it.)

proof.text: **Step 3 (degree $0$: $P(0)$, and sections over quasi-compact opens).** Let $(\mathcal G_i,\gamma_{i'i})$ be a directed system of $\mathcal O_X$-modules over $I$ with colimit $(\mathcal G,(g_i)_i)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-directed-colimit-underlying-sets] the underlying sheaf of sets of $\mathcal G$, with the maps underlying the $g_i$, is a colimit of the underlying sheaves of sets of the $\mathcal G_i$. Let $V\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open. By Step 2, $V$ has a cofinal system of finite open coverings with quasi-compact pairwise intersections, so [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-directed-colimit-sections] (1) and (2) apply to $V$: $(\ast)$ every $t\in\mathcal G(V)$ is $g_{i,V}(s)$ for some $i$ and $s\in\mathcal G_i(V)$; and if $s\in\mathcal G_i(V)$ has $g_{i,V}(s)=0=g_{i,V}(0)$ then (clause (1) with $s'=0$, $i'=i$) $\gamma_{i''i,V}(s)=\gamma_{i''i,V}(0)=0$ for some $i''\ge i$. Transporting along the natural isomorphisms $\theta$ of Step 1 (iii) ($\theta\circ H^0(V,g_i)=g_{i,V}\circ\theta$, $\theta\circ H^0(V,\gamma_{i''i})=\gamma_{i''i,V}\circ\theta$, $\theta$ bijective and additive) gives (a) and (b) for $H^0(V,-)$. Hence $P(0)$. Statement $(\ast)$ and its injectivity companion, for sections over arbitrary quasi-compact opens $V$, are used again in Step 7.

proof.text: **Step 4 (a system of injectives).** Let $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})$ and $(\mathcal F,(c_i))$ be as in the statement. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-functorial-injective-embeddings] there are a functor $J$ and a natural transformation $j:\mathrm{id}\to J$ on $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ with every $j_{\mathcal A}$ a monomorphism into an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Put $\mathcal I_i=J(\mathcal F_i)$, $\psi_{i'i}=J(\varphi_{i'i})$ and $\alpha_i=j_{\mathcal F_i}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal I_i$; then $(\mathcal I_i,\psi_{i'i})$ is a system over $I$ of injective $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\psi_{i'i}\alpha_i=\alpha_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}$. In the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\pi_i:\mathcal I_i\to\mathcal Q_i$ be a cokernel of $\alpha_i$. For $i\le i'$, $\pi_{i'}\psi_{i'i}\alpha_i=\pi_{i'}\alpha_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=0$, so there is a unique $\chi_{i'i}:\mathcal Q_i\to\mathcal Q_{i'}$ with $\chi_{i'i}\pi_i=\pi_{i'}\psi_{i'i}$; uniqueness (as $\pi_i$ is an epimorphism) gives $\chi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\chi_{i''i'}\chi_{i'i}=\chi_{i''i}$, so $(\mathcal Q_i,\chi_{i'i})$ is a system over $I$. Each $0\to\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\alpha_i}\mathcal I_i\xrightarrow{\pi_i}\mathcal Q_i\to0$ is short exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] ($\alpha_i$ a monomorphism, hence a kernel of its cokernel in an abelian category), and for $i\le i'$ the triple $(\varphi_{i'i},\psi_{i'i},\chi_{i'i})$ is a morphism of short exact sequences.

source.place: Cohomology, proof of Lemma 01FF, lines 3222-3240 (Injectives, Lemma 01DI; the short exact sequences 0 -> F_i -> I_i -> Q_i -> 0)

proof.text: **Step 5 (the colimit sequence).** By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-coproduct-finite-subsums] (1) the systems $(\mathcal I_i,\psi_{i'i})$ and $(\mathcal Q_i,\chi_{i'i})$ have colimits $(\mathcal I,(c^{\mathcal I}_i))$ and $(\mathcal Q,(c^{\mathcal Q}_i))$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Since $(c^{\mathcal I}_i\alpha_i)_i$ is a cocone on $(\mathcal F_i)$ ($c^{\mathcal I}_{i'}\alpha_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=c^{\mathcal I}_{i'}\psi_{i'i}\alpha_i=c^{\mathcal I}_i\alpha_i$) and $(c^{\mathcal Q}_i\pi_i)_i$ one on $(\mathcal I_i)$, there are unique $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I$ and $\pi:\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q$ with $\alpha c_i=c^{\mathcal I}_i\alpha_i$ and $\pi c^{\mathcal I}_i=c^{\mathcal Q}_i\pi_i$; then $\pi\alpha c_i=c^{\mathcal Q}_i\pi_i\alpha_i=0$ for all $i$, so $\pi\alpha=0$ by uniqueness. Thus for every $i$ the triple $(c_i,c^{\mathcal I}_i,c^{\mathcal Q}_i)$ is a morphism from $0\to\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal I_i\to\mathcal Q_i\to0$ to the complex $0\to\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal I\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal Q\to0$.

**Step 6 ($0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$ is exact; checked on stalks).** Let $x\in X$, with stalks and stalk maps as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-filtered-colimit] (the directed set $I$ viewed as a filtered category), $(\mathcal F_x,((c_i)_x)_i)$ is a colimit of $(\mathcal F_{i,x})$ in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules, and likewise for $\mathcal I_x$, $\mathcal Q_x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (with $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$) these cocones satisfy hypotheses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion], which (with $R=\mathbf Z$) shows that they are also colimits of the underlying diagrams of abelian groups. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5), each $0\to\mathcal F_{i,x}\to\mathcal I_{i,x}\to\mathcal Q_{i,x}\to0$ is exact (exactness at each of its three inner places is exactness of $0\to\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal I_i$, $\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal I_i\to\mathcal Q_i$, $\mathcal I_i\to\mathcal Q_i\to0$, true by Step 4), the transition maps $(\varphi_{i'i})_x,(\psi_{i'i})_x,(\chi_{i'i})_x$ make these a diagram over $I$ of exact sequences of abelian groups (taking stalks is compatible with composition), and by Step 5 the maps of the colimit sequence are $\alpha_x,\pi_x$ ($\alpha_x(c_i)_x=(c^{\mathcal I}_i)_x(\alpha_i)_x$, $\pi_x(c^{\mathcal I}_i)_x=(c^{\mathcal Q}_i)_x(\pi_i)_x$; the colimit of the constant diagram $0$ is $0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] (Stacks 00DB), $0\to\mathcal F_x\xrightarrow{\alpha_x}\mathcal I_x\xrightarrow{\pi_x}\mathcal Q_x\to0$ is exact. As this holds for every $x$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5) shows that $0\to\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal I\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal Q\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: Cohomology, proof of Lemma 01FF, lines 3247-3255: 'We may check this on stalks. By Sheaves, Sections 009D and 009E taking stalks commutes with colimits. Since a directed colimit of short exact sequences of abelian groups is short exact (Algebra, Lemma 00DB) we deduce the result.'

proof.text: **Step 7 (the claim: $H^q(V,\mathcal I)=0$ for every quasi-compact open $V$ and $q\ge1$).** Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-cech-vanishing-basis] to the $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal I=\varinjlim\mathcal I_i$, with $\mathcal B$ the set of quasi-compact opens of $X$ (a basis by hypothesis (1)) and $\mathrm{Cov}$ the set of coverings $\mathcal U:U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ of the Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site] with $J$ finite and $U$ and all $U_j$ quasi-compact opens. Hypothesis (1) of that node holds by Step 2 (i), hypothesis (2) by Step 2 (ii). For (3), let $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$ and $p\ge0$. The Cech term [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=\prod_{t\in J^{p+1}}\mathcal G(U_t)$ is a finite product, every $U_t$ being quasi-compact (Step 2 (i)). The maps $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,c^{\mathcal I}_i)$ (componentwise $c^{\mathcal I}_{i,U_t}$) form a cocone on the diagram $i\mapsto\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)$ of abelian groups and commute with the Cech differentials, morphisms of sheaves commuting with restrictions. This cocone satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] (with $R=\mathbf Z$): (1) given $z=(z_t)_t\in\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$, Step 3 $(\ast)$ applied to the system $(\mathcal I_i)$ and the quasi-compact opens $U_t$ gives $i_t$ and $y_t\in\mathcal I_{i_t}(U_t)$ with $z_t=c^{\mathcal I}_{i_t}(y_t)$; as $J^{p+1}$ is finite and $I$ directed (and nonempty), pick $i\ge$ all $i_t$, and then $z$ is the image of $(\psi_{ii_t}(y_t))_t$; (2) if $y\in\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)$ maps to $0$, each $c^{\mathcal I}_i(y_t)=0$, so by Step 3 some $i_t\ge i$ has $\psi_{i_ti}(y_t)=0$, and for $i'\ge$ all $i_t$ the image of $y$ in $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_{i'})$ is $0$. Hence $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ is the colimit of the $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)$ in abelian groups, compatibly with the differentials. Each $\mathcal I_i$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module, so by [lem-weil-pbc-module-injective-open-cover-cech-acyclic] (Stacks 01EP) $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)=0$ for $p>0$, i.e. $\check{\mathcal C}^{p-1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)\to\check{\mathcal C}^{p+1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)$ is exact for $p\ge1$; these sequences form a diagram over $I$ (the $\psi_{i'i}$ induce maps of Cech complexes), and by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] (Stacks 00DB) the colimit sequence $\check{\mathcal C}^{p-1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^{p+1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ is exact, i.e. $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for $p\ge1$. So [lem-weil-pbc-module-cech-vanishing-basis] gives $H^q(V,\mathcal I|_V)=0$ for every quasi-compact open $V$ and every $q\ge1$.

proof.text: **Step 8 (the comparison diagram).** Fix a quasi-compact open $U$ and $n\ge0$, and write $H^m(h)$ for $H^m(U,h)$. By Step 1 (i) applied to the short exact sequences of Steps 4 and 6, the rows $H^n(U,\mathcal I_i)\xrightarrow{H^n(\pi_i)}H^n(U,\mathcal Q_i)\xrightarrow{\delta_i}H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal F_i)\to H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal I_i)$ and $H^n(U,\mathcal I)\xrightarrow{H^n(\pi)}H^n(U,\mathcal Q)\xrightarrow{\delta}H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal F)\to H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal I)$ are exact; $H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal I_i)=0$ by Step 1 (ii) ($\mathcal I_i$ injective) and $H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal I)=0$ by Step 7, so $\delta_i$ and $\delta$ are surjective and $\ker\delta=\operatorname{im}H^n(\pi)$, $\ker\delta_i=\operatorname{im}H^n(\pi_i)$. By the naturality in Step 1 (i), applied to the morphisms of short exact sequences $(c_i,c^{\mathcal I}_i,c^{\mathcal Q}_i)$ (Step 5) and $(\varphi_{i'i},\psi_{i'i},\chi_{i'i})$ (Step 4): $H^{n+1}(c_i)\circ\delta_i=\delta\circ H^n(c^{\mathcal Q}_i)$ and $H^{n+1}(\varphi_{i'i})\circ\delta_i=\delta_{i'}\circ H^n(\chi_{i'i})$; functoriality of $H^n(U,-)$ gives $H^n(\pi)H^n(c^{\mathcal I}_i)=H^n(c^{\mathcal Q}_i)H^n(\pi_i)$ and $H^n(\chi_{i'i})H^n(\pi_i)=H^n(\pi_{i'})H^n(\psi_{i'i})$. (This is the diagram of the source, with its two zeros in the right column.)

source.place: Cohomology, proof of Lemma 01FF, lines 3257-3274 (the diagram, the zero at the upper right from injectivity of the I_i, the zero at the lower right from the claim)

proof.text: **Step 9 ($P(n)\Rightarrow P(n+1)$: the snake-lemma chase written out).** Assume $P(n)$; it applies to the systems $(\mathcal I_i,\psi_{i'i})$ and $(\mathcal Q_i,\chi_{i'i})$ with colimits $\mathcal I$, $\mathcal Q$, on the same $U$. Notation of Step 8. (a) Let $x\in H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal F)$. As $\delta$ is surjective, $x=\delta(y)$ with $y\in H^n(U,\mathcal Q)$; by $P(n)$(a) for $(\mathcal Q_i)$, $y=H^n(c^{\mathcal Q}_i)(y_i)$ for some $i$, $y_i\in H^n(U,\mathcal Q_i)$; then $x=\delta H^n(c^{\mathcal Q}_i)(y_i)=H^{n+1}(c_i)(\delta_i(y_i))$. (b) Let $y\in H^{n+1}(U,\mathcal F_i)$ with $H^{n+1}(c_i)(y)=0$. As $\delta_i$ is surjective, $y=\delta_i(z)$ with $z\in H^n(U,\mathcal Q_i)$. Then $\delta(H^n(c^{\mathcal Q}_i)(z))=H^{n+1}(c_i)(y)=0$, so $H^n(c^{\mathcal Q}_i)(z)=H^n(\pi)(w)$ for some $w\in H^n(U,\mathcal I)$. By $P(n)$(a) for $(\mathcal I_i)$, $w=H^n(c^{\mathcal I}_k)(w_k)$ for some $k$ and $w_k\in H^n(U,\mathcal I_k)$; choose $l\ge i,k$ and put $w_l=H^n(\psi_{lk})(w_k)$, so that $w=H^n(c^{\mathcal I}_l)(w_l)$, and $z_l=H^n(\chi_{li})(z)$. Then $u=z_l-H^n(\pi_l)(w_l)\in H^n(U,\mathcal Q_l)$ satisfies $H^n(c^{\mathcal Q}_l)(u)=H^n(c^{\mathcal Q}_i)(z)-H^n(\pi)H^n(c^{\mathcal I}_l)(w_l)=H^n(\pi)(w)-H^n(\pi)(w)=0$. By $P(n)$(b) for $(\mathcal Q_i)$ there is $m\ge l$ with $H^n(\chi_{ml})(u)=0$, i.e. $H^n(\chi_{mi})(z)=H^n(\pi_m)\big(H^n(\psi_{ml})(w_l)\big)$. Hence $H^{n+1}(\varphi_{mi})(y)=H^{n+1}(\varphi_{mi})\delta_i(z)=\delta_mH^n(\chi_{mi})(z)=\delta_mH^n(\pi_m)(\ldots)=0$, as $\delta_m\circ H^n(\pi_m)=0$ by exactness. So (a) and (b) hold in degree $n+1$ for every quasi-compact $U$ and every system: $P(n+1)$.

source.place: Cohomology, proof of Lemma 01FF, lines 3273-3277: 'The top row is exact by an application of Algebra, Lemma 00DB. Hence by the snake lemma we deduce the result for q = q_0 + 1.' (the chase replaces the colimit of the top rows and the snake lemma, with the same content)

proof.text: **Step 10 (conclusion).** By Step 3, $P(0)$ holds, and by Step 9, $P(n)$ implies $P(n+1)$; by induction $P(q)$ holds for all $q\ge0$, which is (a) and (b) for every quasi-compact open $U$. By the elementwise description of the directed colimit of abelian groups [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups] (every element is represented at some stage; an element represented at stage $i$ is $0$ if and only if it becomes $0$ at some later stage), (a) says that the canonical map $\varinjlim_iH^q(U,\mathcal F_i)\to H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ is surjective and (b) that it is injective, so it is bijective.
